title: A Leakage Bound for Confidence Sets after Black-Box Selection
summary: In many analyses the object reported at the end is not fixed in advance, but is chosen after a preliminary search over variables, subgroups, transformations, models or contrasts. Classical selective-inference methods are most effective when this search can be written as an explicit selection event. This note treats the less structured case in which the selection rule is a black box and inference is required for the target indexed by the selected object.
